Once upon a time, there was a big crocodile. He had tough skin and sharp teeth. One day, he went to the river to swim. He saw a ball and tried to bite it, but it was too tough. He decided to roll it with his nose instead.

The ball rolled and rolled until it hit a tree. A little boy came to get his ball. He saw the crocodile and got scared. But the crocodile just wanted to play with the ball. The boy and the crocodile played together, rolling the ball back and forth.

From that day on, the crocodile and the boy became friends. They would play together every day by the river, rolling the ball and having fun. And the crocodile was happy to have a friend who was not afraid of his tough skin and sharp teeth.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Sarah who was three years old. She was playing near the beach when she noticed a reef in the distance. She wanted to see it better, so she ran to it.

When she reached the reef, she was amazed by how many fish there were around it. She also noticed the sharp, jagged rocks which were poking up from beneath the water. It was very loud and she could hear the sound of the waves crashing against the reef.

Sarah was mesmerized. She stayed there for a while and observed the different creatures swimming around the reef. Suddenly, she tasted something strange on her tongue - it was salty and bitter. She put her finger in her mouth and realized it was the taste of the ocean!

Sarah liked the taste and enjoyed looking at the reef. She thought it was so special and couldn't wait to come back and explore more.

Once upon a time, there was a little orange bird named Sunny. Sunny loved to fly around and sing songs. One day, while Sunny was flying, she saw a big, scary cat. The cat wanted to catch Sunny and eat her for dinner!

Sunny was very scared, so she flew to her friend's house. Her friend's name was Lucky, and he was a wise old owl. Sunny told Lucky about the cat and asked him what to do. Lucky told Sunny to lay low and stay safe until the cat went away.

Sunny listened to Lucky's advice and stayed in her nest until the cat left. She learned that when she was in danger, it was important to stay safe and not take unnecessary risks. From then on, Sunny always remembered to be careful and to listen to wise friends like Lucky.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her daddy. One day, they went to the park and it started to rain. Lily's daddy picked her up and they ran to a big tree for shelter. The rain was deep and they got very wet. But they still had fun together, playing and laughing until the rain stopped. From that day on, Lily always loved to play in the rain with her daddy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He loved to eat food and he always enjoyed it. One day, his mom took him to a park. He was happy to be out in the fresh air and play.

At the park, he saw lots of other children playing with toys. Some children had a ball and others had a kite. The little boy also wanted something fun to play with. His mom gave him a toy car that was very useful.

He loved the car and had lots of fun playing with it. He drove it across the grass and pretended to go on an adventure. After a while, it was time to go home. The little boy was sad to leave the park, but he knew the toy car would still be useful the next day.

He and his mom stopped to get some food on the way home. It was so yummy and the little boy enjoyed it. He thanked his mom for the fun day and for taking him to get food. He was happy to be home with his toy car and to have enjoyed some delicious food.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Jacob. Jacob loved to jump and play. Every day he would jump in the sunshine. One day as Jacob was jumping, he saw something tidy in the sun. It was a kite.

Jacob ran up to the kite, but a girl was already there. She had short brown hair and was wearing a pretty pink dress.

Jacob smiled at the girl and said, "Can I play?"

The girl shook her head. "This is my kite. You can't have it," she said.

Jacob was sad. He wanted to play with the kite. He thought for a moment, then said, "Can I come jump with you?"

The girl's face brightened. "Of course you can!" she said.

So Jacob and the girl jumped and played in the sun with the kite. They laughed and jumped until it was time to go home. Jacob had a great day and was happy to have made a new friend.

Once there was a little boy called Tom. Tom was three years old and very happy. One day he had a surprise - his mummy gave him a big present! Tom was so excited and thanked his mummy with a big hug.

The present was wrapped up very carefully in bright paper and Tom wanted to know what was inside. He carefully unwrapped the paper, but it was taking a long time.

So Tom waited patiently and eventually his present was revealed! It was a beautiful bird cage with a little bird inside! Tom was so happy.

The bird was so delicate and fragile and Tom knew he had to be careful with it. He thanked his mummy again and promised to look after the little bird always.

Once there was a stubborn little boy called Paul. He had a special cap that he wore every day. One day, he was playing in the garden when suddenly he started to blink his eyes. He blinked so much that he couldn't see! He was so scared and confused.

Paul's mother saw what was happening and ran to help him. She tapped her finger on his eyes and said "blink, blink little one!". And so Paul blinked and his eyes felt better.

He was so relieved and quickly put his cap back on his head. From that day on, he remembered to blink his eyes every time they get tired. Because he was so stubborn and kept his cap on, he was able to remember this lesson and never forget it!

Once there was a crab who was very sad. Her shell was blue and she didn't like it. She really wanted it to be different, but she did not know how.

One day she asked her friends what she should do, "I really hate my blue shell, " she said. Her friends tried to help her, but they could not think of a way to make it more colorful.

The crab decided to use her imagination. She thought of something that could make the blue shell much more beautiful. She took some colored rocks and put them around her shell.

The crab was so happy! She looked like a beautiful piece of art. Everyone was so proud of the crab and all of them said, "There is nothing more wonderful than a creative crab with a colorful shell!"

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went outside to play. He loved to run and jump and have fun. But today was a little different because it was raining outside. Timmy didn't mind though, he loved to play in the wet rain.

As he was playing, Timmy saw a sign that said "Caution: slippery when wet". But Timmy didn't pay attention to the sign and kept playing. He ran and jumped and had so much fun, until he slipped on the wet ground.

Timmy fell down and hurt himself badly. He realized he should have listened to the sign and been more careful. From that day on, Timmy always paid attention to signs and made sure to be safe when playing outside.

Once, there was a thick animal. It lived in a forest full of trees and sunshine. One day, a little bird flew to the animal and whispered in its ear. The bird told the animal it had to leave the forest. The animal was sad, but it knew it had to go.

So, the animal took one last look at all the beautiful trees and flowers and began to leave. It walked and walked until it came to a big lake. Here the animal stopped and looked around. The lake was so much bigger and thicker than the forest.

The animal found a little boat, floating in the water. It climbed inside and floated away from the shore. The animal sailed away, across the big lake and never looked back. It was heading off on a new adventure and it was feeling brave and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little seed. The seed was very small and it was buried deep in the ground. One day, the sun shone very bright and the rain fell very hard. The little seed felt very happy because it knew it was time to bloom.

Slowly, the little seed started to grow. It grew and grew until it became a big, beautiful flower. The flower was very happy and it started to dance in the wind. Suddenly, a bee came zooming by and landed on the flower. The flower was very happy to see the bee because it knew the bee would help it make more flowers.

But one day, the weather turned very cold and everything became icy. The flower started to shiver and it was very sad because it knew it would not bloom again until the weather became warm. But the little seed inside the flower knew that one day it would bloom again and it felt happy knowing that.

Johnnie was very excited because he was about to go for a ride on his lovely zoom! He grabbed his mysterious helmet and happily leapt onto the seat.

"Ready to go?" He asked his friend Susie.

"Ready!" She grinned, hopping onto the back seat.

Johnnie pressed his foot onto the pedal and the zoom flew off. The wind blew against their faces and the sun was blazing in the sky.

But then, disaster almost struck! Johnnie's zoom stumbled over a bump in the road. He squeezed the brakes and managed to stay in control.

Susie clapped her hands. "That was close!" She exclaimed.

Johnnie smiled. He was determined to make sure they had a lovely ride. So, he slowly and carefully rode around the bump the next time they passed.

Johnnie and Susie waved their hands in the air and laughed all the way home. All in all, it was a lovely ride.

One day, a boy named Tim found a box of junk in his room. In the box, he saw a fragile toy car. It was red and shiny. Tim wanted to race the toy car with his friends. He thought it would be fun.

Tim went outside to play with his friends. They all had toy cars too. They wanted to race their cars to see who was the fastest. But Tim's toy car was fragile. He was scared it might break if he raced too fast.

The race began, and all the cars went fast. Tim's fragile car went slow at first, but then it went faster and faster. In the end, Tim's car won the race. His friends were happy for him. Tim learned that even a fragile car can win a race if you believe in it.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Jack. He was very excited because it was time to hurry to the library. He loved to go there to read books. His favorite was a special black novel.

Jack and his mom ran to the library as fast as they could. When they finally arrived, Jack hurried to the shelves to find his novel. He was so excited to see it sitting high up on the shelf.

Jack and his mom asked the librarian if he could get a chair to reach the book. The librarian kindly got him a tall chair and Jack quickly climbed up. He grabbed the black novel and hurried back down.

Jack and his mom thanked the librarian and rushed back home. Jack couldn't wait to read the new novel. He knew that no matter what stories were contained within the book, his day was sure to be a magical one!

Once upon a time, there was a friendly bear. He liked to eat cereal for his breakfast every day. One morning, he changed his cereal and he tried a new one. The bear liked the new cereal a lot! He enjoyed it so much that he decided to change his cereal every day. He ate different kinds of cereal and discovered he really liked them. The bear was happy eating his new cereal and it made him feel friendly. He smiled every day as he ate his cereal. The end.

Once there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was a very tidy little girl and enjoyed tidying her room. One sunny day she decided to tidy her room even more. She took a prune from her special jar and started to notice a funny thing. As Daisy waved the prune around in the air, it started to disappear! Daisy couldn't believe her eyes. "Where did it go?" Daisy exclaimed.

Suddenly, Daisy heard a voice. It was coming from behind the door. It was her Grandma. Grandma said, "Daisy, I know what happened to the prune. I used my magic to make it disappear. Now use your magic to tidy your room!"

Daisy was so excited. She waved her hands around her room and in a flash everything became tidy. Daisy laughed with joy and thanked Grandma for her help.

The prune never turned up again, but Daisy knew it was in a special place. She learned that with a little magic, Daisy could make anything tidy and disappear!

Once upon a time there was a rat named Sam. He was a very shy rat, and he wanted to make some friends.

One day he saw a fake mouse in the room. He thought it looked like fun, so he decided to try and record it.

He scurried over and grabbed the mouse. The fake mouse said, "Stop!"

Sam was so startled he dropped the mouse and ran away.

The fake mouse laughed, "You don't have to be scared, I won't hurt you. You were just trying to record me, weren't you?"

Sam was embarrassed, but he nodded his head.

The fake mouse said, "Why don't you come back and record me? I think we could be friends."

Sam was so happy and he raced back to get the mouse. They had a great time recording each other, and soon enough, Sam had made a new friend.

The end.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big tree with many leaves. They want to climb the tree and see what is up there.

"Come on, Ben, let's go up the tree!" Anna says.

"OK, Anna, but be careful. The tree is very old and the bark is rough," Ben says.

They hold on to the branches and go up the tree. They see many birds and squirrels and bugs. They also see a hole in the trunk. They are curious and look inside.

"Wow, look, Ben, there is a book in the hole!" Anna says.

"A book? In the tree? Let me see!" Ben says.

They take out the book and open it. The book has many pages with strange words and pictures. The pages are yellow and torn. The cover is leather and has a metal lock.

"This book is very old, Anna. Maybe it is ancient. I wonder who put it here and why," Ben says.

"Maybe it is a magic book, Ben. Maybe it has secrets and spells and stories," Anna says.

They look at the book and try to read it. They do not understand the words, but they like the pictures. They see dragons and fairies and castles and stars.

"This book is amazing, Anna. I wish we could keep it," Ben says.

"Me too, Ben. But maybe someone is looking for it. Maybe it belongs to someone who loves it very much," Anna says.

They think for a while. Then they decide to put the book back in the hole. They close the cover and lock it with the metal lock. They hope the book is safe and happy in the tree.

"Goodbye, book. Thank you for letting us see you," Anna says.

"Goodbye, book. Maybe we will see you again someday," Ben says.

They climb down the tree and go back to their parents. They do not tell anyone about the book. They keep it as a secret in their hearts. They always remember the book and the tree and the adventure they had.

Once there was a good girl who loved hugs. She hugged everyone and everything she could. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. She got so excited that she ran fast and accidentally fell down. But all of her friends came to hug her and made her feel better. She knew that she was still good and that her friends always loved to hug her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with a long hall. One day, Lily was walking down the hall when she heard a loud noise. It was her cat, Mittens, playing with a toy.

Lily felt happy because she loved her cat. Mittens ran up to her and licked her hand. Lily felt Mittens' soft fur and smiled. She picked up Mittens and carried her down the hall to her room.

Lily loved her home and how it made her feel. She felt safe and happy there. She cuddled with Mittens and felt grateful for her loving family. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jenny and she had a tire. She liked to bounce and roll it around the garden. One day, she rolled it too fast and it went away from her! She watched as it rolled further away until it stopped. Jenny was scared but she knew she had to get it back.

She chased after the tire but it was impossible for her to catch it. She looked around and found some help from a big animal. It was a horse! The horse was nice and it offered to help her.

The horse galloped after the tire and soon Jenny saw it stop. The tire was very fragile and the horse was careful not to break it. Jenny was relieved and thanked the horse. She grabbed the tire and the horse gave her a ride back home.

That night, Jenny hugged her tire and said thank you. She had learned an important lesson - never surrender when it comes to something you love.

Once upon a time, there was a messy little boy named Tim. Tim liked to play in the snow. One day, he went outside to play with his friends. They made snowballs and threw them at each other. Tim was having so much fun.

While they were playing, Tim saw a big snowman. He wanted to pinch its nose. Tim thought it would be funny. He walked up to the snowman and pinched its nose very hard. But the snowman's nose was not soft. It was very cold and icy.

Tim's hand hurt a lot. He started to cry. His friends came to see what was wrong. They told Tim not to pinch the snowman's nose again. Tim's hand was very cold and red. He went home feeling sad. The snowman's nose was still there, but Tim learned not to pinch it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard, where she had a big tree with lots of branches to climb. One day, while she was playing, she saw a raven sitting on a branch. The raven looked at Lily and said, "Hello little girl, can you bring me some food?"

Lily was surprised that the raven could talk, but she wanted to help. She went inside and brought some bread crumbs. The raven ate them and said, "Thank you, you are a dependable friend."

From that day on, Lily would bring food for the raven every day. They became good friends and would talk for hours. One day, the raven said, "Lily, I have to go now. But I will always remember you as my dependable friend."

Lily was sad to see the raven go, but she knew they would always be friends. She looked up at the tree and smiled, knowing that her new friend would always be there, even if she couldn't see him.

Lily and Max liked to play with chalk. They drew big pictures on the sidewalk. They made flowers, stars, and cars. They used many colors. They were happy.

But then, a big dog came. The dog was brown and furry. He barked loud. He ran fast. He saw the chalk pictures. He wanted to play too. He jumped on the sidewalk. He scratched the pictures with his paws. He destroyed the chalk.

Lily and Max were sad. They cried. They said, "Go away, dog! You are bad! You ruined our pictures!"

The dog did not understand. He thought they were playing. He licked their faces. He wagged his tail. He wanted to be friends.

Lily and Max stopped crying. They looked at the dog. He was cute. He was sweet. They petted him. They said, "OK, dog. You can stay. But you have to be nice. You can't destroy our chalk."

The dog nodded. He barked softly. He was sorry. He wanted to be nice. He helped them draw new pictures. He made a heart, a bone, and a dog. He used his nose. He was happy. Lily and Max were happy too. They played with chalk and the dog. They had fun. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars. He had a red car, a blue car, and a green car. Timmy's mom asked him to wash his hands before dinner. Timmy went to the bathroom to wash his hands, but the faucet was broken. Water was splashing everywhere! Timmy's mom came to see what was wrong. "Oh no! This is serious," she said.

Timmy's mom tried to fix the faucet, but she couldn't. Timmy had an idea. "Mom, can we use the hose outside to wash our hands?" he asked. "That's a great idea, Timmy," said his mom. They went outside and turned on the hose. The water was coming out really fast, like a race car! "Wow, this is speeding water!" said Timmy.

Timmy and his mom washed their hands with the speeding water. They laughed and had fun. Then, they went inside for dinner. Timmy was happy that he could help his mom fix the faucet problem.

Once upon a time, there was a little caterpillar named Tim. Tim had a small body and he wanted to gain a beautiful body. Tim had a lot of friends, but he wanted to be like the pretty butterflies that flew in the sky.

One day, Tim decided to ask his friend, the wise old owl, how he could gain a beautiful body. The wise old owl told Tim that he needed to eat lots of leaves and then take a long nap. Tim was excited and started to eat many leaves. He ate and ate until he was full.

Tim then found a nice branch and took a long nap. When he woke up, he felt something was different. Tim looked at his body and saw that he had gained a beautiful body with big, colorful wings. Tim was now a butterfly! He was so happy and flew around showing his beautiful new body to all his friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Millie. She was three years old and loved to explore the world around her. Millie's mom was very rich and had bought her a microscope. Millie loved it and she spent all her free time looking at things through the microscope.

One day, Millie had a bright idea. She wanted to borrow her mom's microscope and take it to school to show her friends. She ran over to her mom and asked,

"Mom, can I borrow your microscope?"

Her mom looked a bit surprised but replied,

"Sweetheart, borrowing the microscope is a big responsibility. Are you sure you can handle it?"

Millie was sure she could handle it and promised to be extra careful. Her mom said okay but warned her that if anything happened to the microscope, she would have to buy a new one.

Millie was so excited to take the microscope to school and show off to her friends. Little did she know that this decision would lead to a big conflict later on.

When the day was over, Millie was unable to find her microscope. It had gone missing! She searched the school for it but it was nowhere to be found.

Once upon a time, there was a rail. It was so long, the end couldn't be seen! One day, a little girl wanted to manage it. She wanted to find out where it went! So off she went, walking down the rail.

It seemed like a long journey. Everything was dull and boring, until, oops! The girl slipped and slid right off the edge of the rail. She got back up and kept walking.

But then she saw something. What was it? It was a big, bright button! She pressed it, and all of a sudden, the rail started to move! It was so cool! The girl was thrilled!

The little girl had managed the rail! She got to ride on it and see where it went. When the ride was over, she was so proud of herself! She had managed the rail by herself.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a big bag with toys and snacks. They zip the bag and go to the park.

They see a big slide. They want to slide down. Lily goes first. She slides fast and laughs. Ben goes next. He slides faster and louder. But he slides too fast. He falls off the slide and hurts his knee. He cries.

Lily runs to Ben. She sees his knee. It has a red patch. She says, "Oh no, Ben, you have a boo-boo. It must hurt. Do you want a hug?"

Ben nods. He hugs Lily. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. Can you help me?"

Lily says, "Yes, I can help you. Let's go to the bench. I have a band-aid in the bag. I can put it on your patch. It will make it better."

They go to the bench. Lily zips the bag and takes out a band-aid. She puts it on Ben's patch. She says, "There, now you have a nice band-aid. It has a star on it. You are brave, Ben."

Ben smiles. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are kind, Lily. The band-aid is nice. It has a star. I like stars. Do you want a snack?"

Lily says, "Yes, I want a snack. What do you have?"

Ben says, "I have cookies. They are tasty. They have chocolate chips. Do you like chocolate chips?"

Lily says, "Yes, I like chocolate chips. They are yummy. Can I have a cookie?"

Ben says, "Yes, you can have a cookie. Here, take one. We can share. We are friends."

They take a cookie each. They bite the cookie. They say, "Mmm, tasty!"

They eat the cookie. They smile. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a black cat named Mittens. One day, Lily's mom asked her to tie her shoes. Lily tried and tried, but she couldn't do it.

"Mama, can you tie my shoes?" asked Lily.

"Sure, sweetie," said her mom.

While her mom was tying her shoes, Lily noticed that the fridge was open.

"Mama, the fridge is open!" exclaimed Lily.

"Oh no! Thank you for telling me, Lily," said her mom as she closed the fridge.

Lily and her mom went on their way, with Lily's shoes tied and the fridge closed. Mittens followed along, happy to be with his favorite girl.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to design pretty dresses for her dolls. One day, she decided to design a special dress for her mommy's tea party.

Lily's mommy was very excited to see the dress Lily had designed. She poured some tea for herself and her friends and they all sat down to enjoy the party. But after a while, Lily started feeling dizzy and had to lie down.

Her mommy realized that Lily had forgotten to eat something before the party and gave her some cookies. Lily felt better and was able to join the party again. Everyone complimented her on her beautiful dress and she felt very proud of herself.

From that day on, Lily always made sure to eat something before attending a party. She also continued to design beautiful dresses for her dolls and her mommy's tea parties.

The little girl was so excited. She was getting ready to play a new game, and she just couldn't wait! The rules were simple: when someone says "surrender", you have to quickly run over to a chair and sit down.

Her friends all raced around the room, and the little girl was very fast. She watched as her friends found a chair and sat in it. Everyone was having so much fun.

Even though the game was exciting, the little girl wasn't sure if she wanted to surrender yet. She ran and ran, but nobody said the word. Suddenly, a loud shout rang through the room -- "Surrender!"

The little girl froze and then quickly sprinted towards a chair. She was the first one to sit down! Everyone cheered and the little girl smiled. She was so happy that she had won the game.

The little girl was excited to play again tomorrow. She knew that she would be even faster the second time around!

Once upon a time, there was a boy. He dreamed of being wise. One day, he found a white egg in the forest. He thought it was so special that he took it home.

The next day, the egg hatches, and out came a snowman! The little boy was so excited that the snowman was alive.

The snowman was kind, and full of wisdom. He told the boy stories and taught him important lessons.

One day it was so cold outside, the snowman started to freeze! The little boy wanted to save his new friend, so he made a plan. He grabbed all of his warm blankets and wrapped the snowman up tightly.

The snowman stayed warm and safe. From then on, the boy and snowman shared special adventures, and the little boy was always learning new wisdom!

Once there was a family who was all ready to sail. The mother and father, and their three year old daughter. They went out to the sea, and their boat bobbed up and down in the water. They had a sail and a flag, too.

The wind was just right and the family set sail. The little girl could see the sea on either side. As they sailed, the ocean was so wide and beautiful.

The family sailed for a little while and then suddenly a huge wave came along! It knocked the boat and the family was ready to stay balanced. Luckily, everything was okay.

The family sailed and sailed and sailed, exploring different places. Finally they decided to go home. They put up their sail, and and headed back to the harbor. They were glad they had a safe and wonderful journey.

Lily liked to play with her mom's comb. It was shiny and had many teeth. She used it to make her hair look pretty. Sometimes she pretended it was a magic wand or a sword.

One day, she found the comb on the table in the living room. She picked it up and ran to her room. She wanted to play with it alone. She closed the door and locked it. She did not want anyone to bother her.

She put the comb on her bed and looked for her dolls. She wanted to comb their hair too. But she could not find them. They were hidden under the blanket. She lifted the blanket and saw them. She smiled and grabbed them.

She heard a knock on the door. It was her mom. She said, "Lily, open the door, please. I need the comb. It is mine, not yours."

Lily did not want to give the comb back. She liked it too much. She said, "No, mom. It is mine. I found it. Go away."

Her mom said, "Lily, that is not nice. You have to share. The comb is not a toy. It is for brushing hair. If you do not open the door, I will be angry."

Lily felt scared. She did not want her mom to be angry. She did not want to make her sad. She thought for a moment. She decided to be good. She said, "Sorry, mom. I will open the door. Here is the comb. You can have it."

She unlocked the door and gave the comb to her mom. Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good girl. I love you."

Lily felt happy. She said, "I love you too, mom. Can I play with the comb later?"

Her mom said, "Yes, you can. But only if you ask me first. And only if you are careful. OK?"

Lily said, "OK, mom. I will ask you first. And I will be careful."

They both smiled and went to the living room. They played with the comb and the dolls together. They had fun.

Once there was a brave little boy called John. He had big blue eyes and a funny pointy nose. One day, he wanted to race his friends. He ran so fast that he was the winner. After he raced, he was smiling from ear to ear. He was so proud of himself for being so brave and running so fast.

The next week, John had a race against his classmates. He was excited and raced as fast as he could. His nose was scrunched up as he ran and he shouted, "I'm going to win!"

John was so determined, he won the race. His friends cheered for him and he was so happy. He had been very brave. He was the fastest and they all applauded his effort.

John learned that day that no matter what, if you are brave and try your best, you can do great things.

Once upon a time, there was a big red ball. The ball loved to bounce all day. One day, the ball saw a pretty stamp on the ground. The stamp had a picture of a happy sun. The ball wanted to play with the stamp.

The ball bounced over to the stamp. It bounced higher and higher, trying to pick up the stamp. But the ball could not hold the stamp. The ball felt ashamed. It wanted to show the stamp to its friends. The ball had an idea.

The ball bounced very high in the sky. It landed on the stamp with a big "boing!" The stamp stuck to the ball. The ball was happy. It bounced all the way home to show the stamp to its friends. They all loved the stamp and played together.

Once there was a family who had a very intelligent boy. His name was Andy. Every day, Andy would use the faucet in the bathroom and play a game. He would press his tiny hand to the faucet and watch as the water came out like magic.

One day, Andy wanted to make something special from the faucet. He tried and tried, but nothing worked. He was very disappointed.

Suddenly, an idea came to him! He ran to his parents and asked them for some paper. His parents gave him a roll of paper and he ran back to the faucet. He put the paper under the faucet and pressed the handle. Water started to flow and it made beautiful shapes. Andy smiled and laughed.

He had learned a new way to use the faucet. He had made something special. He had printed a picture with the faucet!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mom. Lily saw a butterfly and wanted to catch it. Her mom said, "Be careful, Lily. We have to protect the butterfly."

Lily saw a boy playing on the slide. He was very loud and not being quiet. Lily's mom said, "Let's go play somewhere else. It's too noisy here."

Lily and her mom found a quiet spot to play. They saw some kids playing a game. One kid said, "I want to win every time!" Lily's mom said, "It's not fair to always win. Everyone should have a turn to win."

Lily had a lot of fun at the park that day. She learned that it's important to protect animals, be quiet when needed, and play fair with others.

Lily and Max were restless. They wanted to play outside, but it was raining. They looked around the house for something fun to do. They saw a big box in the corner of the living room.

"What is in there?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Let's find out!" Max said.

They opened the box and saw many old things. There were books, toys, clothes, and pictures. They searched the box for something interesting. They found a shiny medal, a soft hat, a broken watch, and a yellow letter.

"Look at this!" Lily said, holding the letter. "It has a name on it. Grandma Rose."

"Who is Grandma Rose?" Max asked.

"I don't know. Maybe she was Mom's mom or Dad's mom. Let's ask them!" Lily said.

They ran to the kitchen, where Mom and Dad were making lunch. They showed them the letter and the other things.

"Wow, where did you find these?" Mom asked.

"In the big box in the living room. Who is Grandma Rose?" Lily asked.

Mom smiled and hugged them. "Grandma Rose was my mom. She died when I was little. She was very brave and kind. She gave me this medal when I was born. It was from her time in the army. She wrote me this letter before she went away. It tells me how much she loves me and how proud she is of me. It is the truth."

Lily and Max looked at the letter and the medal. They felt sad and curious.

"Can we read the letter?" Max asked.

"Of course. I will read it to you. And then we can look at the pictures and I can tell you more stories about Grandma Rose. She would have loved to meet you." Mom said.

Lily and Max nodded. They followed Mom to the couch and sat with her. They listened to her voice and looked at her face. They felt happy and warm. They learned more about Grandma Rose and their family. They forgot about the rain and the boredom. They found something more fun and important. They found the truth.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went for a walk in the forest. He saw a turkey walking around. The turkey was harmless and didn't hurt anyone. Timmy loved animals, so he followed the turkey to see where it was going.

Suddenly, the turkey sprang up into a tree! Timmy was surprised and amazed. He had never seen a turkey do that before. The turkey looked down at Timmy and made a funny noise. Timmy laughed and waved at the turkey.

After a while, the turkey climbed back down and continued walking. Timmy decided to go home and tell his mommy about the turkey that sprang up into a tree. From that day on, Timmy loved turkeys even more because he knew they could do cool things like spring up into trees.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient tree. It was very old, even older than Grandma! One day, the tree heard some news. It was so excited to know! The news said that a big party was going to happen! The tree was so happy, it started to dance and sing! Everyone around was so surprised to see the tree dance! Everyone laughed and danced with it. The ancient tree was so happy! The party went on for hours and hours until it was time for the tree to go to bed. Everyone said goodbye and thanked the tree for the wonderful day. The ancient tree knew it had enjoyed a very special day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy cube that she loved to play with. It was red and blue and had letters on it.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. They saw some ducks in the pond. Lily wanted to feed them, so her mommy gave her some bread. Lily broke the bread into little pieces and threw them to the ducks. The ducks were happy and quacked loudly.

As they were leaving the park, Lily noticed that the sky was getting dark. She looked up and saw a bright light shining in the sky. It was a shooting star! Lily made a wish and closed her eyes tightly. She wished for a new toy cube to play with. When she opened her eyes, the shooting star had disappeared. But Lily felt happy and excited anyway.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went on a train ride with her mommy. They went through a long, dark tunnel that was very noisy. "Mommy, I don't like this tunnel. It's too noisy," said Lily.

"I know, sweetie. But we'll be out of it soon," replied her mommy.

As they came out of the tunnel, Lily noticed something was missing. "Mommy, where's my teddy bear? I miss him," she said with a sad face.

"Don't worry, Lily. We'll find him. Let's ask the train conductor for help," said her mommy.

So, they asked the train conductor and found Lily's teddy bear. Lily was very happy and hugged her teddy bear tightly. They continued their train ride and had a great time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little fly. The fly had a tight hat on his head. He liked to look at the big world around him.

One day, the fly met a big dog. The dog said, "Hi, little fly! I like your tight hat. Can you show me how to look at the world like you do?"

The fly said, "Yes, big dog! Just look up, look down, look left, and look right. You will see many things."

The big dog looked up, down, left, and right. He saw a pretty flower, a green tree, and a blue sky. The big dog was happy. He thanked the little fly for teaching him how to look at the world. They became good friends and looked at the world together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and make things with her hands. One day, she decided to design a special hat for her teddy bear. She used colorful paper and glue to make it just right.

Later that day, Lily went to a meeting with her friends. They were going to have a picnic in the park. When they saw Lily's bear with the unusual hat, they all wanted one too! So, Lily helped her friends design their own hats.

Everyone had a great time at the picnic, wearing their unique hats and playing games. Lily felt happy that she could share her love of creating things with her friends. From that day on, they had many more meetings where they designed and made things together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her garden. One day, she saw that the vine in her garden was broken. She went to her mom and said, "Mommy, the vine is broken. Can we fix it?"

Her mom said, "Of course, we can fix it. We just need some tools." They went to the shed and got some tools. Her mom showed her how to use them. Lily felt so modern using the tools.

Together, they fixed the vine and Lily was so happy. She said, "Thank you, mommy. Now the vine looks beautiful again." Her mom replied, "You're welcome, Lily. It's always good to fix things when they are broken."

From that day on, Lily loved to fix things in her garden. She felt like a modern gardener. And whenever something was broken, she would say, "Let's fix it!" just like her mom taught her.

Once upon a time, there was a goat named Billy. Billy was very adventurous and loved to explore the fields. One day, Billy met a funny friend who made him laugh. They played together and had so much fun.

As they were playing, they saw a big hill. Billy wanted to climb it, but he was scared. His friend encouraged him and they climbed the hill together. When they reached the top, they saw a beautiful view and laughed with joy.

From that day on, Billy and his friend went on many adventures together. They laughed and played and had the best time ever. Billy was so happy to have a friend who was just as adventurous as he was.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with flowers and grass. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side.

They ran up the hill, holding hands. They were happy and excited. But then, Ben stumbled on a rock and fell down. He hurt his knee and cried. Lily stopped and ran back to him. She saw blood on his knee and felt scared.

"Ben, are you okay?" she asked. She hugged him and tried to make him feel better.

Ben sniffed and nodded. He looked at his knee and saw a fly on it. He shooed it away and said, "Go away, fly. You are not nice. You want to eat my blood."

Lily saw the fly too and said, "Yes, go away, fly. You are not our friend. You are mean and dirty."

The fly buzzed and flew away. It did not like to be shooed. It looked for another place to land. It saw a flower with nectar and flew to it. It was hungry and thirsty.

The flower was happy to see the fly. It said, "Hello, fly. You are welcome here. You can drink my nectar and help me make seeds. You are my friend. You are nice and helpful."

The fly was surprised and happy. It said, "Thank you, flower. You are very kind. You have sweet nectar and beautiful petals. You are my friend. You are pretty and grateful."

The fly and the flower became friends. They talked and shared. They helped each other and smiled.

Ben and Lily saw the fly and the flower. They saw that they were friends. They felt sorry for shooing the fly. They realized that the fly was not mean and dirty. It was just different and hungry.

They said, "Sorry, fly. We were wrong. You are not bad. You are good. You have a friend. We are happy for you."

The fly and the flower said, "Thank you, Ben and Lily. You are not bad either. You are good. You have each other. We are happy for you too."

Ben and Lily smiled and hugged. They felt better. They said, "We are sorry for our knee. We are happy for our friend. We are grateful for our park."

They climbed the hill again and saw what was on the other side. They saw more flowers and flies and friends. They played and laughed and learned. They had a good day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside every day. One day, Lily's mom told her they were going to have a picnic at the park. Lily was so excited!

As they were getting ready, Lily's mom reminded her to pack her toys and snacks. "Remember to be organized, Lily," she said. Lily nodded and promised to be organized.

When they arrived at the park, Lily saw her friends playing. She ran over to join them, but soon realized she forgot her toys. "Oh no!" she cried. "I forgot my toys!"

Her mom reminded her about being organized, but Lily was too upset to listen. Her friends shared their toys, but Lily was sad she didn't have her own.

Later that day, Lily's mom took her for a jog around the park. As they were jogging, they saw a little boy who didn't have any toys to play with. Lily remembered how sad she felt earlier and decided to share her toys with the boy. The little boy was so happy and thanked Lily.

Lily learned that being organized is important, but sharing and kindness is also important. She felt happy knowing she made someone else's day better.

Once upon a time there was a sweet little girl. She was very creative and could come up with ideas all the time. She loved to draw and sing.

One day, she found a big box. She tried to open it, but it was locked. She looked around, but she couldn't find the key.

She held up her hands and asked her mom, "Can you help open this box?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Let's try to be creative and find the key."

The girl looked around the room and found a paperclip. She put the paperclip in the lock and it opened.

Inside the box was a beautiful doll. The girl was so happy that she jumped up and down. She held the doll in her hands and hugged it tightly.

She thanked her mom for her help. Together, they laughed and enjoyed the happy moment.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big sister named Sarah. One day, Lily asked Sarah if she could have a cookie from the cupboard. Sarah said, "Sure, but be careful not to make a mess."

As Lily reached for the cookie jar, she accidentally knocked over a cup and it broke. Sarah scolded her and said, "Now we have to clean up this mess."

Suddenly, it started to rain outside. Lily looked out the window and said, "Look, it's raining! Can we go play in the rain?" Sarah replied, "No, it's too ugly outside. We'll have to wait for it to stop raining."

Lily was sad, but she knew her big sister was always right. So, they cleaned up the mess and waited for the rain to stop. When it finally did, they went outside and had fun jumping in puddles. The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and smell them. Lily saw a daisy that was very pretty. It had white petals and a yellow middle. She wanted to pick it and give it to her mom.

"Look, Ben, a daisy!" she said. "Can I have it?"

Ben looked at the daisy. He saw that it was modest. It did not show off like the roses or the sunflowers. It was happy to grow in the grass and share its beauty with the bees and the butterflies.

"Maybe you should leave it, Lily," he said. "It is happy here. If you pick it, it will die."

Lily thought about it. She loved her mom, but she also loved the daisy. She did not want to make it sad.

"OK, Ben, I will leave it," she said. "But can we come back and see it again?"

"Sure, Lily, we can come back," he said. "But we have to be gentle and not step on it or pull it."

They smiled and waved at the daisy. Then they ran to play with the ball. The daisy smiled back and thanked them for being kind.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved his green sweater very much. One day, Timmy's mommy washed his sweater and forgot to put it in the dryer. When Timmy went to put on his sweater, he saw that it was still wet and he felt sad.

Timmy's mommy said, "Don't worry, Timmy. We can manage to dry your sweater quickly." She took the sweater and put it on a hanger. Then, she hung the sweater outside in the sun to dry.

After a while, Timmy's mommy checked on the sweater and saw that it was still wet. She said, "Oh no, the sweater is still empty of dryness." But then she had an idea. She brought the sweater inside and put it in the dryer.

When the dryer was finished, Timmy's mommy gave him his sweater and it was warm and cozy. Timmy was happy again and he hugged his mommy. From that day on, Timmy made sure to remind his mommy to put his sweater in the dryer so it wouldn't be empty of dryness again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved sausages and he always wanted to eat them. One day, Timmy went to the park with his mom and saw a little girl crying. He went to her and asked what was wrong. The little girl said that someone pinched her toy and she couldn't find it.

Timmy felt sad for the little girl and wanted to help her. He looked around the park and found the toy. He gave it back to the little girl and she stopped crying. Timmy felt incredible because he made the little girl happy again.

Timmy learned that it's important to be kind and help others. He also learned that it's not nice to take things that don't belong to us. From that day on, Timmy always tried to be helpful and kind to everyone he met.

One cold winter morning, Jenny got up and had an urge to study. She asked her mom, "Can I study?" Her mom said, "Yes! What would you like to learn?" Jenny said, "I want to learn about animals!" Her mom smiled and said, "Let's look it up!" They went to the computer and read about all kinds of animals. Jenny was excited to learn something new and her urge to study kept growing. They studied about wild cats, big bears, and funny monkeys. Jenny had so much fun learning, she didn't want to stop! With her mom's help, Jenny knew so much more about animals than before. It was a cold and fun day of study!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park with her mom and dad. One day, they went to a park with a big fountain in the middle. The water shot up high in the sky and then fell down like rain.

Lily watched the water spin around and around in the fountain. It was so fast, she could hardly keep up with it. She laughed and clapped her hands with joy. Suddenly, she wanted to spin around too!

So, she held onto her mom's hand and started to spin around and around. It was so much fun! When they stopped, she felt dizzy but happy. Lily loved the fountain and the way it made her feel. She couldn't wait to come back and spin again another day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old and loved adventures. One day, Amy found a secret chamber in her backyard. Anxious to explore, she opened the door of the chamber. Suddenly, Amy heard a loud rumble. When she looked inside, she saw a huge monster!

The monster shouted, "I will destroy you!". Amy was scared but bravely said, "No, you won't!". The monster became angry and charged towards her.

She ran outside and shouted for help. Then, her parents heard her cry and quickly came outside. They saw the monster and shouted, "Go away!". The monster was scared and ran away.

Amy was relieved and hugged her parents. From that day onwards, she always thought twice before exploring any mysterious chambers.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy called Will. He was just 3 years old and very curious about the world. Every day he asked lots of questions about what he saw and talked to everyone he met.

One day, Will was playing outside when he saw a lovely tree in the distance. He decided to go over and talk to it, so he carefully walked up to it.

But when he got there, the tree didn't answer him like Will was expecting. He thought he'd been silly for thinking it could talk.

Will was very sad and disappointed, but he didn't give up. He told the tree that, if it was too shy to answer, it could always talk to the birds and the bees, instead. Then he decided to go home.

The next day, when Will returned, he saw that the tree was fully in blossom! Will couldn't believe it! The tree had clearly taken his advice and was talking to the birds and the bees.

Will was so happy that his idea had worked, and he realized that words can be great, if we use them with care and kindness!

Once upon a time, there was a boat that liked to sail. She was a big boat and she liked to glide through the water. The boat sailed all the time, day and night, in rain and in sunshine.

One day, there was a big storm at sea. The boat was tossed around, tossed and turned in the big waves and it was a lot of fun. But after a while, it got tired so the boat pulled into a harbour to rest.

When the boat stopped, it noticed the water was sour. It made a funny face, like it tasted something yukky. The boat decided to go somewhere else to sail.

It glided away, out of the harbour and into the sunshine. There was no sour taste in the water and the boat was happy. It sailed around, in and out of the waves, for a long time.

The boat sailed until it reached a beautiful bay, with lots of seagulls and a tiny beach. Finally, it had found the perfect place to take a break from sailing.

The boat rested and sailed, sailed and rested, until it was time to sail away again.

Once upon a time there was a lonely volcano. He lived up on a high hill in the middle of a vast, deserted valley. Every night, he would sit on the hilltop and look out into the dark, empty landscape.

The volcano felt terribly lonely and wanted some company. One night, he found a voice. It was arguing with itself. When the volcano asked who was talking, the voice replied that it was only a small bird.

The bird had been flying around all night looking for a place to rest. But the volcano made too much noise so the bird kept on flying. The volcano felt sorry for the bird and invited it to stay with him on the hilltop.

The bird accepted, and the two of them talked until the sun began to rise. The bird told the volcano stories of its travels and the volcano listened. Every night when the sun went down, the volcano and the bird would talk until morning came.

Then one night, instead of talking, the bird started to complain about how cold and lonely it was up on the hilltop. The volcano felt terrible. He was so sorry to hear the bird complain and wanted to make things better.

The volcano said to the bird that it could come and stay in the big hollow beneath his peak. The bird accepted, and from then on, the volcano and the bird were friends. The lonely volcano had a companion and was never alone again.

Once there was a young girl who felt very miserable. She was so sad that she wanted to rest. She found a quiet spot in the back yard and curled up in a ball. She stayed there for a long time, close her eyes, and rested. She felt slightly better afterwards, but not quite back to her old self. However, she knew she would eventually feel better with some more rest. So, she decided to crawl away to a sunny patch of grass and closed her eyes again. After a few moments, she felt much better! Her misery had gone away and she was happy once again. All she needed was a bit of rest.

John saw his mother. He thought she was so smart. His mother seemed so happy and neat. She was wearing a big red ribbon in her hair.

John's mother was always teaching him. She taught him shapes, colours, and counting. She read him stories and sang him songs.

John knew his mother was the smartest of them all. He wanted to be just like her.

John was so proud. He was learning everything quickly. It seemed like he was getting smarter every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing with her favorite toy, a red ball. Suddenly, her little brother Jack came and took her ball. Lily was very upset and started to cry.

"Jack, give me back my ball!" Lily said.

"No, I want to play with it now," Jack said.

Lily didn't want to share her ball because she was afraid Jack would break it. Jack didn't understand why Lily was so upset, he was ignorant of her feelings.

"Please hurry and give it back to me, Jack," Lily said.

Jack finally understood that he had upset his sister and gave her back the ball. Lily was happy again and they played together. From that day on, Jack learned to be more careful with Lily's objects and they never had another conflict again.

Once upon a time, there was a young engine. He was so excited to explore the world. One day, he was in the sun and it had started to get very warm. The engine began to melt. He melted and melted until there was nothing left of him.

The engine was so sad that he had melted away. He wished he could go out and explore the world. Then, one day, something magical happened.

A young girl came along and saw the melted engine. She was very creative and she had an idea. She took some materials from the ground and started to build the engine a brand new body!

When she was finished, the young engine was amazed. He looked around and saw a brand new world that he could explore. He thanked the young girl for bringing him back to life.

The young engine was so happy. He could start his adventure and explore the world.

The end.

Once upon a time there were two best friends called Max and Sammy. They were always playing together in a park which had a big well. Sammy knew that it was not safe to play by the well, but Max was very curious. One day, when they were playing together, Max opened the well. Suddenly, Sammy was so scared that he ran away from the well.

Max called Sammy back and said: "I'm sorry Sammy. I didn't mean to make you scared. Can we still be best friends?"

Sammy looked at Max and smiled. Then he said: "Yes, I forgive you. Let's go play somewhere else."

So, Max and Sammy promised to be best friends and left the well. Ever since that day, they promised to never go near the well again.

Once upon a time there was a family who loved going on adventures. One day they decided to go camping.

Mum said, "We need to prepare for our camping trip!"

Dad said, "Let's get the tent, food and games ready."

The little girl smiled, she was so excited to go!

On the way to their camping spot, they stopped at a river. Suddenly, the little girl saw a very unusual word written in the sand.

The little girl asked: "What does that word mean?"

"It's a surprise," mum said.

When the family got to their campsite, the little girl looked back at the word in the sand and shouted with joy, "It's the name of the river!"

Mum laughed and said, "That's right! Now, let's prepare for a wonderful camping adventure!"

Once there was a little boy called Tommy. He wanted to find something he liked to eat. He looked in the kitchen and he found an onion. He was curious to taste it. So he picked it up and took a bite.

At first he thought it would taste funny, but it was actually very yummy. He liked it so much he wanted to try some more. He put the onion in his mouth and it tasted even better.

Tommy was so happy, he ate the whole onion! He kept saying how yummy it was. His mum came in and saw how he was enjoying the onion. She said it was a good idea and now they make onion meals all the time and it's Tommy's favourite food.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside in the dirt. One day, he found a long, wiggly worm. The worm was very friendly and liked to play with Tim.

"Hi, worm!" said Tim. "Do you want to play with me?" The worm wiggled and danced, and Tim knew that it wanted to play too. They played together all day, digging in the dirt and making new friends with the other worms.

Tim had an expensive toy car. It was big, red, and shiny. Tim liked to play with his car, but he was always careful not to break it. One day, while playing with his worm friend, Tim accidentally drove his car too fast and it hit a big rock. The car broke into pieces.

"Oh no!" said Tim. "My car is broken. What should I do?" The friendly worm wiggled and danced, and it gave Tim an idea. Tim picked up the pieces of his car and put them back together. With the help of his worm friend, Tim fixed his expensive toy car.

Tim was so happy that his car was fixed. He thanked his worm friend and they continued to play together. From that day on, Tim knew that he could always count on his worm friend to help him when things got tough. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a kind lady named Mrs. Smith. She wore a big apron and liked to bake yummy treats. One day, she went to her garden to pick some fresh vegetables. She was very humble and always shared her crops with her neighbors.

As she was picking some carrots, she noticed a little bunny hopping around. The bunny was so cute and Mrs. Smith wanted to pet it. But the bunny was scared and ran away. Mrs. Smith didn't want to scare the bunny, so she left it alone and went back to her kitchen to bake some carrot cake.

Later that day, Mrs. Smith brought the cake to her neighbor's house. The neighbor was so happy and said it was the best cake she had ever tasted. Mrs. Smith felt proud and happy that she could make someone else smile. From that day on, Mrs. Smith always made sure to pick extra vegetables for her neighbors and share her delicious treats.

Once upon a time, there was a big tower. It was very tall and had lots of windows. One day, a powerful wizard came to the tower. He wanted to set up his magic shop inside.

The wizard had a big hat and a long beard. He had a wand that could do amazing things. He used his wand to set up his shop. He made sure everything was in the right place.

Soon, people came from all over to see the wizard's magic shop. They were amazed by his powerful spells. The wizard was happy to help them all. And the tower became a very special place, full of magic and wonder.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to wander. Everywhere she went she found something new and exciting, but today she was in a meadow, looking for something special. She spotted a pale fork in the grass and knew at once what it was. She picked it up, excited by the new find, and started to wander again.

The meadow was very big and it seemed to stretch on forever. The little girl wandered and wandered until the sun started to set. She was getting very tired and knew she had to go home soon. Suddenly she spotted something beautiful in the sky, a big rainbow that shone brightly! She was so happy and started to run back home, the pale fork still in her hand.

When she got home she showed her mom the pale fork and told her about the wonderful rainbow she had seen. Her mom was amazed by the pale fork and gave her a big hug. From then on the little girl kept the pale fork in a special box so she could remember the fun day she had spent wandering in the meadow.

Tom is a big boy who likes to help his dad. Every morning, he wakes up early and goes with his dad to the shop. His dad sells newspapers to people who want to read them. Tom thinks his dad is very successful, because he has many customers and always smiles.

One day, Tom sees a big truck outside the shop. The truck has many newspapers inside. The driver says he is late and he needs to rush. He asks Tom and his dad to help him unload the newspapers. Tom is excited and says yes.

Tom and his dad work hard and fast. They take the newspapers from the truck and put them in the shop. They make a big pile of newspapers. Tom feels proud and happy. He says to his dad, "Look, dad, we did it! We helped the driver!"

His dad hugs him and says, "Yes, Tom, we did it! You are a great helper! I am very proud of you!" He gives him a newspaper and says, "This is for you. You can read it later and learn new things."

Tom smiles and says, "Thank you, dad! I love you!" He holds the newspaper and looks at the pictures. He thinks he will be a successful newspaper seller like his dad when he grows up.

Once there was a small worm called Bob. Bob was very playful and loved running around and exploring. One day, Bob found himself in a brand new garden. He wriggled around and explored all the colourful flowers.

Suddenly, out of nowhere, a little girl appeared. She bent down and looked into Bob's eyes. Bob hoped he wouldn't be squished.

The little girl smiled and said, "You're so cute! I'm going to love you!"

Bob was so happy and bounced around in joy. The little girl laughed and decided to pick him up carefully and take him home with her. From then on, the little girl and Bob were the best of friends and played together every day.

Tom and Sue were excited to go to the park with Mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They also liked to look at the birds, the flowers and the big trees.

One day, they saw a new path in the park. It was narrow and rocky, and it went up a hill. Mom said they could explore it, but they had to be careful and stay close to her. Tom and Sue agreed, and they followed Mom up the path.

The path led them to a cliff. It was very high and steep, and they could see the river and the bridge far below. Tom and Sue were amazed by the view. They wanted to see more, so they walked closer to the edge of the cliff.

"Look, Mom, look!" Tom shouted. "I can see a boat and a fish and a duck!"

"Be careful, Tom, don't go too close!" Mom warned. "The cliff might break and you might fall!"

But Tom did not listen. He took one more step, and then he heard a loud crack. The ground under his feet broke, and he started to slide down the cliff. He screamed and reached for Mom.

Mom was quick and brave. She grabbed Tom's hand and pulled him back to safety. She hugged him and scolded him. "Tom, you were very naughty and foolish! You could have hurt yourself or worse! You have to listen to me and follow the rules!"

Tom was scared and sorry. He cried and said, "I'm sorry, Mom, I'm sorry! I won't do it again, I promise!"

Sue was also scared and sorry. She hugged Tom and said, "I'm sorry, too, Mom. I should have stopped Tom. I love you, Tom, and I don't want you to get hurt!"

Mom was relieved and glad. She hugged them both and said, "I love you, too, Tom and Sue. I'm happy you're both safe and sound. But you have to be more careful and sensible next time. Now let's go back to the park and have some fun!"

Max was at the airport with his mom and dad. His eyes lit up when he saw the airplanes. He had always wanted to try flying one. So he asked his parents if he could fly one. They said no. He felt sad.

Suddenly, Max noticed a man at the airport who knew how to fly planes. He went up to the man and asked if he could fly a plane. The man paused, then smiled and said yes.

Max was so excited. He followed the man to the plane. He asked the man lots of questions. The man answered honestly. He told Max all about the controls and buttons.

Max got into the plane and was about to fly it when suddenly the man revealed a big problem. He said the plane was not ready. Disappointment revealed in Max's face. He wouldn't be able to fly the plane today.

But the man had an idea. He said that if Max came back tomorrow, then he could fly the plane. Max was so excited! He thanked the man for being so honest. He headed home to get ready for his big day at the airport tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to explore and play outside. He always wanted to find out what was beyond the gate. One day, the little boy was so brave and he decided to open the gate. He was very excited to see what was there!

But as the boy opened the gate, he felt a pinch on his arm. He quickly closed the gate and started to cry.

An old man came up to the boy and asked, "What's wrong, little one?" The boy told the old man what happened and the old man said, "Don't worry. You were very brave to open the gate, but you also have to be patient. Next time you should think before you open the gate. That pinch was probably a bee or something else that can hurt you. Be patient, and don't jump into new adventures until you make sure it's safe."

The boy smiled and nodded. He was thankful for the old man's advice and promised never to open the gate before taking a deep breath and being patient.

Moral of the story: Always take a deep breath and be patient before trying something new.

Grandma took Sally to school one day. Sally looked around as she entered the classroom. It was gray, and had lots of desks in it. Grandma asked her, "did you like this classroom Sally?". Sally smiled and said "Yes, I like it!".

Grandma and Sally looked around the classroom and saw a big project. It had lots of pieces that needed to be put together. Sally asked, "Grandma, can I complete this project?" Grandma smiled and said, "of course you can!"

Sally began to carefully put the pieces together. She carefully cut, glued and added all of the pieces. Finally, she had completed the project. Grandma clapped proudly and said, "great job Sally. You did it!"

Sally smiled with pride and said "I completed it!". Grandma and Sally hugged and packed up their things to go home. Sally felt happy that she had completed the project.

Once there was a boy who always wanted to do what was best. He had an idea to make everyone happy. He suggested that everyone should share their toys. Everyone seemed to like the idea and even smiled.

But then, one day when it was really hot, the boy wanted to play with all the toys by himself, in the shade. He wanted to keep the toys all to himself. So, he told everyone that they couldn't have their toys anymore.

The other kids got angry, and no longer wanted to be nice to the boy. They were very sad and it turned out that his suggestion made everyone feel worse.

The moral of the story is to always think carefully before suggesting something. Even if your idea is a good one, it can make people unhappy if you don't think carefully.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play basketball. He was a good player and loved to shoot the ball into the hoop. One day, he went to the park to play with his friends. It was a hot day and the sun was shining bright.

Timmy's friend, Johnny, came up to him and asked, "Hey Timmy, can I play too?" Timmy said, "Sure, but we need to squeeze the ball to make sure it's not too flat." They squeezed the ball and started to play. Timmy was happy to have his friend playing with him.

After a while, Timmy's team was winning and Johnny was getting upset. He said, "It's not fair, you guys are too good." Timmy replied, "Don't worry, it's just a game. Let's keep playing and have fun." Johnny felt better and they continued to play until the sun went down. They were tired but happy, and Timmy felt lucky to have such a great friend to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety wanted to go on a journey to see the world. So, Tweety asked his mommy if he could go on a journey. His mommy said yes and she was proud of Tweety for being brave.

Tweety packed his bags and started his journey. He flew over mountains, rivers, and forests. He saw many different animals along the way. He even saw a big, yellow, friendly dog who wanted to play.

When Tweety arrived at his destination, he wanted to send a message to his mommy to tell her about his journey. He found a post office and sent a postcard to his mommy. His mommy was so proud of him for going on a big adventure.

One day, a kind little girl named Lily went to the park. She saw a lost dog. The dog was sad. Lily wanted to help the dog return home.

Lily asked the dog, "What is your name?" The dog said, "My name is Max." Lily said, "Let's find your home, Max!" They walked and looked for Max's home. They met a big, mean dog. The mean dog did not want them to pass. Lily said, "Please let us pass. We are looking for Max's home."

The big, mean dog saw how kind Lily was. The mean dog felt bad and let them pass. They walked more and found Max's home. Max's family had a surprise for Lily. They gave her a big thank you hug. Lily was happy she helped Max return home.

Once upon a time, there was an old lady who loved flowers. She would go to the garden every day and take care of them. One day, a little girl saw her and said, "Why do you like flowers so much?"

The old lady smiled and said, "Flowers are beautiful and they make me happy. When I see them, I want to applaud!"

The little girl didn't understand what applaud meant, so the old lady clapped her hands and said, "Like this! It means I'm happy and I like something very much."

The little girl thought about it and said, "I like flowers too! Can I help you take care of them?"

The old lady was happy to have some help and they spent the rest of the day planting and watering the flowers. When they were done, the little girl clapped her hands and said, "I'm so happy we did this together! Thank you for showing me how to applaud for flowers."

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She loved to play with her toys. One day, Sarah's Mommy took her to a museum. Sarah had never been to a museum before and was very excited.

When they arrived, Sarah and Mommy saw many different things. Sarah really liked the pictures and statues.

"Mommy, do these things belong in the museum?" asked Sarah.

Mommy smiled and said "Yes, sweetheart. People keep these things in a museum so we can look at them and learn more."

Suddenly, they saw a bad man. He was trying to take something that did not belong to him. Sarah was scared, but Mommy told her that it was okay. The museum guard took the bad man away, and Sarah and Mommy went home.

From that day on, Sarah knew that museums were the perfect place for all the special things that belonged there.

Jamie excitedly ran outside to find a lizard. She had been wanting to see one for a long time. Jamie saw a small, green lizard scurrying along the sidewalk. She was very excited and started chasing after it.

The lizard was pretty fast, but Jamie was determined to catch it. Despite her small size, she managed to catch up with the little lizard and reach out her hands to grab it. Unfortunately, the lizard was very stubborn and managed to escape Jamie's grasp.

Jamie tried again and again to catch the lizard, but each time it was too fast. She eventually gave up and ran back to her house, disappointed.

However, Jamie didn't lose hope. She smiled, knowing that one day she would find a lizard she could catch.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. One day, Tim went to the store with his mom. They bought some spicy food. Tim liked spicy food very much.

On their way home, Tim and his mom needed to take a taxi. They waited and waited for a taxi to come. Finally, Tim noticed a yellow taxi coming their way. They got in the taxi and told the driver where they lived.

As they got closer to their home, the sky turned dark and it started to rain. Tim and his mom ran inside their house. But they forgot the spicy food in the taxi. The taxi drove away, and they never saw the spicy food again. Tim was very sad because he wanted to eat the spicy food.

Once there was a kangaroo who was very nice. He liked to share with his friends. One day the kangaroo found a box of treats. He thought they smelled so good, so he wanted to share them with his friends. He hopped around to find them. But there were no friends to be found.

The kangaroo was sad, so he went to sit under a shady tree. There was a mild breeze and it cooled him from the warm sun. He had a sudden thought! The kangaroo hopped back to the treats and broke some of the treats in half.

He soon found his friends and shared the treats with them. Everyone was so happy! They enjoyed the treats and thanked the kangaroo for sharing with them. Ever since then, the kangaroo has been spreading the joy of sharing wherever he goes.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to work and patch with her dad. One day, Lucy asked her dad for help with a fragile patch.

"Daddy, can you help me patch this?" asked Lucy.

"Sure thing, sweetie," he replied, "but you'll have to be very careful. This patch is very fragile so you'll need to be extra gentle when mending it."

Lucy nodded and slowly worked on the patch with her daddy, taking extra care not to damage it. After a while, their hard work paid off and the patch was as good as new.

Lucy and her dad hugged each other proudly and smiled.

"I'm so glad we could fix it together," said Lucy.

"Me too," said her dad, "We make a good team!"

Once upon a time, there was a mother and her three year old daughter. One day, the daughter had a problem she was facing. She didn't know what to do and was very worried.

The mother told her, "I will support you and make the case easy for you."

The little girl listened to her mother and followed her directions. She soon found the problem easier to solve.

We all need support from our family and friends to make things easier. We should never be afraid to ask for help whenever we have a problem. This is the moral value of this story.

Once upon a time, there was a mother. She was very sad because her favorite toy was broken. It was a top that used to spin round and round. She loved to watch it spin.

One day, her little child found the broken top and wanted to make his mother happy again. He took the top and tried to spin it with all his might. At first, it didn't spin well, but he kept trying.

Finally, the top started to spin faster and faster. The mother watched in amazement as her child made the top spin again. She was no longer sad, but very happy. They both laughed and played with the top, spinning it over and over again.

Tom and Jen are twins. They like to play on the farm with their dad. One day, dad says he has a surprise for them. He takes them to the barn and shows them two baby cows. One is brown and one is black.

"Which one do you want to keep?" dad asks. "You can choose one each."

Tom likes the brown cow. He thinks it is cute and soft. He gives it a hug and says, "I choose this one. I will name it Brownie."

Jen likes the black cow. She thinks it is strong and brave. She gives it a pat and says, "I choose this one. I will name it Jet."

Dad smiles and says, "Good choices. You can feed them and play with them every day. But remember, they will grow up to be large cows. You have to take good care of them."

Tom and Jen are happy. They thank dad and run to get some hay for their cows. They do not know that Brownie and Jet have a secret. They are not ordinary cows. They are magic cows.

One night, when Tom and Jen are asleep, Brownie and Jet sneak out of the barn. They use their magic to fly over the fields and the woods. They have fun and see many things. They come back before dawn and pretend to be normal cows.

Tom and Jen do not notice anything. They love their cows and their cows love them. But sometimes, they wonder why their cows have sparkles in their eyes and feathers in their fur.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was weird weather. The sun was hot, and then it was cold. The rain came, and then the snow. People did not know what to wear. They were sad.

One day, a little girl named Lily went for a walk. She saw a big tree with a small door. She opened the door and found a magic room. In the room, there was a big button. The button said "return."

Lily pushed the button, and the weather changed. The sun was warm, and the air was cool. The rain and snow went away. The people in the town were happy again. They played outside and had fun.

Every time the weather got weird, Lily would return to the magic room and push the button. The town was always happy because of Lily. They knew they could count on her to fix the weather. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved playing with her dolls. One day, she was playing outside when she saw a big puddle. She wanted to jump in it, but her mom told her not to because it was too cold outside.

Lily decided to play with her dolls inside instead. She picked up her favorite doll, a pretty one with a pink dress, and started playing with her. Suddenly, her little brother came in and wanted to play too.

Lily said, "You can play with my doll, but be careful not to freeze her!" Her brother picked up the doll and started playing with her. But then, he accidentally dropped her and her arm broke off.

Lily got upset and said, "Oh no, my doll doesn't fit anymore!" Her mom came in and saw what happened. She told Lily not to worry and that she could fix the doll's arm. Lily was happy again and thanked her mom for helping her.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Anna. She was very brave. One day Anna wanted to try something new and exciting. She asked her mom for help and her mom said yes!

The mom and Anna went to a store. There were lots of colorful things to see. Anna saw a big needle and stared at it. She wondered what she could do with it.

Her mom said that they could make something special. Anna was very excited and helped pick out some colorful fabric and pretty buttons. When it was time to use the needle, they put safety glasses on Anna and she was ready.

Anna practiced poking the fabric with the needle. She was a natural! She carefully sewed the fabric and added the colorful buttons. When she was done, she had made a beautiful dress. Anna was so proud of her work.

The mom said that the dress was perfect and the two of them had such a fun day together! They were both very thankful for the special needle that helped Anna to create something amazing.
